limitations: The toy engine models each invariant as a single boolean switch; a production engine's invariants can be partially present (e.g. a dedup window with a TTL), which this binary model does not capture.

clean_one_to_one_isolation.checkpoint: NOT isolated -- also defeats duplicate_callback and crash_before_local_record because it is the durable substrate idempotency-key dedup reads from
clean_one_to_one_isolation.idempotency_key: NOT isolated -- also required for safe crash-retry, not only duplicate_callback

real_control_plane_probe.stale_commit_error: stale fence token 1 < 2; refusing commit from evicted worker

reproduction.outcome_rationale: The named invariant set does predict fault survivability (every removal breaks at least the fault class named in the frozen hypothesis), but the mapping is not four independent 1:1 levers as a naive reading suggests. checkpoint is a load-bearing precondition beneath idempotency-key deduplication: removing checkpoint alone silently defeats duplicate-callback and crash-retry protection even though idempotency_key is nominally still 'on', because there is no durable place left to record what was already done. Only fence_token and outbox are cleanly isolated to their named fault class. The real, unmodified control_plane.py (which has all four invariants together) was independently probed in a sandbox and behaved exactly as the FULL row of the toy matrix predicts (stale fence rejected, duplicate commit marked as a no-op replay, zero false completions), so the refined dependency structure is consistent with, not contradicted by, the real live mechanism.
